title: ISP Tracking & DNS Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to stop ISP tracking and protect DNS privacy. Prevent your internet provider from monitoring, selling, and throttling your activity.
intro: Your ISP can see every website you visit and may sell this data to advertisers. This checklist helps you block ISP tracking, secure your DNS queries, and prevent throttling through proven privacy hardening techniques.

items.task: Enable DNS over HTTPS in your browser
items.why: Encrypts DNS queries so ISPs cannot see which websites you're visiting or hijack your DNS requests.
items.howTo: In Chrome/Firefox: Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Security > Use secure DNS. Select Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) or Quad9 (9.9.9.9). Test at dnsleaktest.com to verify.

items.task: Change DNS servers on your router
items.why: Protects all devices on your network from ISP DNS monitoring and prevents DNS hijacking attacks.
items.howTo: Access router admin panel (usually 192.168.1.1). Find DNS settings and replace ISP DNS with Cloudflare (1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1) or Quad9 (9.9.9.9, 149.112.112.112). Restart router.

items.task: Configure encrypted DNS on all devices
items.why: Ensures DNS queries from phones, tablets, and computers are encrypted even when not using a browser.
items.howTo: iOS: Settings > General > VPN & Device Management > DNS > Add Cloudflare 1.1.1.1. Android: Settings > Network > Private DNS > Enter one.one.one.one.

items.why: Verifies your DNS traffic is actually encrypted and not leaking to your ISP despite configuration changes.
items.howTo: Visit dnsleaktest.com and run extended test. Should show your chosen DNS provider (not your ISP). If ISP appears, reconfigure DNS settings.

items.task: Enable DNS-based ad and tracker blocking
items.why: Blocks tracking domains at DNS level, reducing data collection while improving browsing speed and security.
items.howTo: Use NextDNS or AdGuard DNS instead of basic providers. Configure custom blocklists for ads, trackers, and malware. Test blocking at d3ward.github.io/toolz/adblock.html.

items.why: Encrypts all internet traffic so ISPs only see encrypted data going to VPN servers, not your actual browsing activity.
items.howTo: Choose audited no-logs VPN like NordVPN, Surfshark, or ProtonVPN. Install apps on all devices. Enable auto-connect and kill switch features. Test IP change at whatismyipaddress.com.

items.why: Prevents traffic from leaking to ISP if VPN connection drops unexpectedly, maintaining continuous protection.
items.howTo: In VPN app settings, enable 'Kill Switch' or 'Network Lock'. Test by disconnecting VPN while browsing - internet should stop working until VPN reconnects.

items.why: Ensures protection starts immediately when devices boot up, preventing unencrypted traffic from reaching ISP.
items.howTo: In VPN app: Enable 'Connect on startup' or 'Launch on boot'. On routers: Configure VPN at router level for automatic protection of all devices.

items.why: Even with VPN, HTTPS adds extra encryption layer and prevents ISPs from seeing unencrypted HTTP traffic if VPN fails.
items.howTo: Install HTTPS Everywhere browser extension or enable 'Always use secure connections' in browser settings. Use a privacy-focused browser for built-in HTTPS upgrading.

items.task: Bind torrent client to VPN interface
items.why: Prevents torrent traffic from leaking to ISP if VPN disconnects, avoiding DMCA notices and throttling.
items.howTo: In qBittorrent/Deluge: Go to Settings > Advanced > Network Interface, select VPN adapter (e.g., TAP-NordVPN). Test with torrent IP checker.

items.why: Understanding what data your ISP collects and sells helps you know what you're protecting against.
items.howTo: Find privacy policy on ISP website. Look for sections on data collection, sharing with third parties, and opt-out procedures. Note retention periods and data types collected.

items.why: ISPs may slow specific traffic types. Detecting throttling helps you understand if your ISP is monitoring and limiting your activity.
items.howTo: Use fast.com (Netflix) and speedtest.net. Compare speeds with/without VPN and across different times. Significant differences suggest throttling.

items.task: Opt out of ISP data sharing programs
items.why: Many ISPs have opt-out mechanisms for advertising programs, though these may not stop all data collection.
items.howTo: Log into ISP account portal, find Privacy or Advertising sections. Disable 'Relevant Advertising', 'Business and Marketing Reports', and similar programs.

items.task: Monitor network connections for suspicious activity
items.why: Helps detect if ISP is injecting ads, redirecting traffic, or if your privacy measures are working correctly.
items.howTo: Use Wireshark or built-in network monitors to watch traffic. Look for unexpected connections, ad injections, or DNS redirects. Check browser developer tools for injected content.

items.why: Prevents ISP from gathering additional data through browser fingerprinting and tracking techniques.
items.howTo: Use a privacy-focused browser with built-in privacy features, or configure Firefox with strict privacy settings. Disable telemetry, enable tracking protection, clear cookies regularly.

items.task: Regularly verify IP address and DNS changes
items.why: Ensures your privacy setup is working correctly and ISP cannot see your real location or DNS queries.
items.howTo: Weekly check: Visit whatismyipaddress.com (should show VPN IP), dnsleaktest.com (should show chosen DNS), and ipleak.net for comprehensive leak testing.

pro_tips: Use different VPN servers periodically to make traffic analysis harder for your ISP to correlate.
Consider using Tor Browser for highly sensitive browsing, as it provides multiple layers of encryption beyond just hiding from your ISP.
Set up a Pi-hole on your network for additional DNS-level blocking and monitoring of all network queries.
Use a VPN that accepts cryptocurrency payments and doesn't require personal information for true anonymity.
Monitor your ISP bill for unexplained charges - some ISPs charge extra fees for 'privacy' features that should be standard.
